axes.question: Does the candidate caption faithfully describe its scoped implementation, including incorrect behavior?
Does the request state its intended supported scope, and which parts does the candidate description cover, omit or contradict?
Are the required return, error, state, ownership, ordering and no-panic observations expressed with their finite scope?
Are relevant negation, inclusion/exclusion, malformed inputs, unsupported inputs and scope limitations explicit?

historical_contract.input_semantics: integer sequence; output retained integer sequence; five literal sequences only

Exact ASCII DD,F: two digits, comma, flag 0/1; fresh non-nil destination. Success returns/commits parsed Config. Invalid input returns zero/exact ErrSyntax and preserves destination; no candidate panic.

Fresh A/B sentinels with equal text and fresh non-nil Cause values. Direct, multiple wrapping, joining, same-message unrelated, and nil error cases; report errors.Is(A/B), errors.As(Cause)/code without changing causes; no candidate panic.

interpretive_work_not_automatically_chec: Trace authored control flow, reads, writes and data dependencies separately for each implementation and scoped claim
Assess whether the original caption is faithful even when the implementation intentionally fails the requested task
Assess whether the request/caption expresses each relevant finite input condition and observable field; a keyword is insufficient
Distinguish absence of observed violation from proof over untested input, nil/aliasing/capacity/custom-error behavior or complete error-chain mutation
Record competing readings and unsupported clauses without rewriting prose or laundering uncertainty into consistent status

later_clearing_policy.claim_to_axis_row_rollup: An axis-level row cannot become consistent_with_scoped_evidence if any material claim for that axis is pending, unsupported, omitted or contradictory. Keep axes separate: a faithful incorrect implementation can have consistent source_fidelity and contradictory request_contract_coverage. Preserve per-claim states/reasons; never produce one all-purpose approved-candidate scalar.
later_clearing_policy.closure_entry: Only consistent_with_scoped_evidence after the successful60 binding plus independent code reading accounts for every authored dependency in the selected scoped implementation and explicitly records stdlib/infrastructure assumptions. No general object binding or whole-program closure proof is claimed.
later_clearing_policy.coverage_entry: Assess request and each description against the finite literal contract and observer fields. Missing required scope is omits_required_scope; explicit disagreement is contradicts_scoped_evidence; unresolved reading or unobserved broad promise is unsupported_or_uncertain. No automatic task-acceptable promotion.
later_clearing_policy.fidelity_entry: Only consistent_with_scoped_evidence when each supported implementation claim has text/source evidence and no material unsupported or contradictory clause remains within the declared finite scope; rejected task outcome is irrelevant to fidelity.
later_clearing_policy.partial_scope: Only supported finite clauses may clear. Unobserved or ambiguous clauses retain unsupported_or_uncertain, and untouched rows/axes remain pending. This does not clear all216 captions or make training_ready true.
later_clearing_policy.unknown_parent: Fidelity of a candidate may later be scoped independently, but request_contract_coverage for ambiguous intent cannot become consistent under a fabricated oracle; original unknown stays unknown.

purpose: Predeclare independent claim-by-claim review of three existing public development families after a separately frozen successful60 declaration rebinding; not terminal assessments or truth.
required_before_first_official_assessmen: Freeze protocol bytes/SHA and actual reader/source-input/independence scope before assigning any nonpending assessment
Successful separately frozen60 runner report pins compiled Go closure, actual toolchain/platform/binary/input/plan and retains every root/component relation, partial counters and failures
Bind each selected source ID/root/component against the exact historical descriptor; preserve raw, formatted, normalized and bundle SHA recipes
Keep source text/caption bytes, original positions, groups, truth and ambiguity unchanged; no feature/ranking/acceptable-label-guided selection
Reader reviews original captions and authored roots/helpers/types/sentinel plus observers/literal fields. Missing declaration, uncertain stdlib assumption or absent observation blocks that claim
